_readme: Which audit runs when a file changes, read by hooks/audit_on_edit.py, and (for entries marked preCommit) by bin/run_precommit_audits.py. audit_on_edit.py is advisory only — nothing it runs can block a tool call or write a file. run_precommit_audits.py is the opposite on purpose: it is what bin/install_precommit_hook.py wires into .git/hooks/pre-commit (or a .pre-commit-config.yaml local hook), and it DOES fail the commit when a preCommit entry reports something. Only mark an entry preCommit if it is both fast (seconds, every commit) and invariant (a real regression, not a judgment call) — see the field's own description in hooks.map.schema.json. Full field contract: plugins/backend-suite/templates/hooks.map.schema.json. NOTHING here ships with 'preCommit': true, on purpose: a scaffold cannot know which checks a project wants its commits gated on, and a gate they did not choose is a gate they will reach for --no-verify around. Turning one on is a deliberate edit. If an audit is ever listed in backend_suite/engine/audit_discovery.DISABLED it exits 2, and both runners name it 'NOT RUN … disabled' rather than letting its silence read as a pass. Do not register a disabled audit and expect it to check anything. WHAT SHIPS HERE: one real, working entry, not a placeholder. This file used to scaffold a single TODO-shaped entry, which matched nothing, ran nothing, and reported nothing — so a project that installed the suite and never edited this file believed its saves were audited while the runner did exactly nothing. That is the suite's governing failure (an unconfigured check indistinguishable from a clean one) sitting in its own scaffold, so the default is now live on arrival. The shipped entry is audit_error_handling for a measured reason: a hook entry must scope itself to the changed directory, and only the audits that take --dir (currently audit_error_handling, audit_proposal_status, audit_doc_staleness) can; its subject — a client call that bypasses the project's own guard — is a regression, not a judgment call; and it is deterministic. NARROW IT: the shipped glob is keyed on the file EXTENSIONS the shipped language adapters handle (backend_suite/adapters/*.FILE_GLOBS), because a scaffold cannot know this project's directory layout — it deliberately names no directory. Once profile.json's source.root and source.fileGlob are filled in, tighten 'glob' to match them, so an edit outside the source tree stops triggering an audit that has nothing to say about it. BOTH --out AND --findings are redirected to scratch paths, and both are load-bearing: --out keeps a directory-scoped run's raw findings away from the whole-repo artefact /quality-debt grades on (a scoped run must never overwrite a full sweep), while --findings is what actually writes the {"findings": [...]} envelope reportWhen 'findings' reads. An entry that redirects only --out points findingsPath at a bare JSON array the runner cannot read, and reports nothing forever — which is the same silence in a new costume. NO 'fixHint' SHIPS HERE, deliberately: doctor.py's check_fix_hints_are_safe requires every script or skill named as a repair to carry an entry in templates/safe-repairers.json attesting that it cannot destroy work, and no read-only audit skill has earned one yet. A scaffold that shipped an unvetted fixHint would fail doctor on a brand-new project, or — worse — buy its way past the gate with an attestation nobody measured. Add your own fixHint once the thing it names is on that allowlist. Delete the entry (or the whole file) if you genuinely do not want on-save nudges — but note bin/doctor.py reports an absent, empty, or placeholder-only map as a finding, precisely so 'nobody configured this' cannot keep reading like 'everything is clean'.
